header.stance: 油價回落支撐短中期美債，長端漲勢卻未能維持

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開篇固定收益論點

油價下跌協助美國公債以週線上漲作收，但週五盤中的漲幅部分回吐，市場對美伊協議的期待仍未等到實際決定。5年期殖利率下降2個基點至4.13%，10年期持平於4.45%，30年期則微升至4.99%。通膨補償降低，較長天期實質殖利率卻上升，漲勢集中在短端與中期公債。

月底指數調整帶來一波可觀買盤，$3,240億附息公債納入主要美債指數。不過，貿易與存貨數據好壞參半，未能為持續上漲提供同樣強的支持。部分聯準會官員主張暫時不對能源衝擊作出反應，其他官員仍保留緊縮選項；交換市場定價顯示，年底前約有15個基點的升息幅度。

信用市場仍有資金，但借款人取得的條件差異很大。市政債基金吸金，日本銀行資本債受到認購，大型媒體收購案則開始考驗貸款市場及不同評等債券的需求。新興市場整體漲幅不大，尚比亞的買回提案卻帶動個別主權債大漲。歐洲與日本的通膨及即將到來的政策決策，仍讓債市前景難以單憑油價回落判斷。

## 油價帶動的漲勢在長端遇阻

美國總統Donald Trump表示正在召開伊朗相關會議後，美國公債一度上漲，殖利率逼近當週低點。投資人期待中東供給恢復，已將指標油價壓至六週低點；但隨後傳出Trump離開會議、尚未作出最終決定，債券也回吐部分漲幅。30年期殖利率盤中最低來到4.96%，收盤則比低點高3個基點。

WTI下跌1.73%至$87.36，Brent下跌1.77%至$92.05。油價下降減輕近期通膨壓力，但地緣政治結果仍未明朗，投資人沒有持續追高長債。收盤時，2年期殖利率下降1個基點至3.98%，5年期下降2個基點至4.13%，10年期持平於4.45%，30年期上升1個基點至4.99%。2s10s利差擴大1個基點至47個基點，2s30s擴大2個基點至101個基點。5年期表現較佳，使2s5s10s蝶式利差下降3個基點至負17個基點；2s10s30s則維持負7個基點。

10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.38%，實質殖利率卻上升1個基點至2.07%，兩者互抵，使名目殖利率持平。5年期與7年期抗通膨公債實質殖利率分別維持1.61%與1.83%，20年期與30年期則各升1個基點至2.49%與2.71%。與週四由實質殖利率下降帶動的漲勢相比，這次市場主要下調通膨補償。拉長至全週，2、5、10及30年期名目殖利率仍分別下降15、14、11及8個基點，收復部分戰爭引發的跌幅。

4月貿易報告顯示，進出口同時增加。商品貿易逆差初值由修正後的$853億收窄至$824億，小於市場預期的$865億。出口增加$85億至$2,197億，進口增加$56億至$3,021億。逆差縮小有利淨出口對GDP的貢獻，但進口仍增，並未顯示國內需求崩落。

存貨數據則較難得出一致結論。批發庫存增加0.5%，低於預期的0.8%，也不及3月修正後的1.5%；零售庫存增加0.7%，高於預期的0.4%，其中不含汽車部分增加0.6%，汽車經銷商庫存增加0.9%。庫存累積可能支撐近期GDP，最終需求是否跟得上卻仍不明確。

堪薩斯市聯準銀行總裁Jeff Schmid表示，4月PCE物價年增3.8%，通膨仍然過高，官員應保留升降息的彈性。他認為勞動市場大致平衡：勞動人口成長較慢，即使聘僱減速，失業率也可能保持穩定。因此，沒有就業過熱，不代表通膨本身不足以構成升息理由。

Michelle Bowman較傾向暫不回應短暫的能源通膨，擔心額外緊縮會不必要地削弱經濟活動與就業。若衝突延長、油價居高不下，或更廣泛傳導至PCE，判斷就會改變。Mary Daly認為目前不急於調整利率，費城聯準銀行總裁Anna Paulson則將近期情況描述為一連串價格衝擊，尚未看到通膨結構改變的證據。官員的談話讓市場繼續評估衝擊會持續多久，而非得到明確的政策承諾。

被動資金的買盤更為直接。紐約時間下午4點，當月新發行、合計約$3,240億的附息公債納入主要美債指數，規模高於3月與4月底各約$2,400億。基金調整部位使期貨成交量大增，指數調整前後債券上漲，尤其有利中期公債，但價格未能重回盤中高點。

德意志銀行在下午5點稍後發布策略更新，預估10年期殖利率將於12月達到4.70%高點，高於先前接近當時4.45%水準的年底預測。該行認為聯準會已結束降息，之後將維持在長期中性利率附近。這與市場認為年底前約有55%機率升息的看法不同，但兩種情境都限制了殖利率持續下行的空間。

股市收高，S&P 500上漲0.22%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.36%。半導體指數在一週強勢表現後大致持平，VIX下跌2.67%至15.32。美元指數下降0.11%至98.91，減輕美元借款人的部分壓力。黃金則上漲1.36%至$4,560.50，即使股市上漲、波動率降低，對地緣政治與通膨不確定性的避險需求仍在。

## 資金需求穩健，信用條件各有不同

信用債基金溫和上漲，LQD升0.09%、HYG升0.10%，JNK升0.16%。短期融資維持穩定，國庫券附息等值殖利率介於3.68%至3.79%，4至52週各天期單日變動均不超過1個基點。初級市場認購金額可觀，但吸引投資人的理由，取決於收益、資本結構與供給稀缺程度。

截至5月27日的一週，美國免稅債券基金淨流入約$23億，接近前一週的兩倍，為1992年以來第二大單週流入，其中市政債ETF約占$17億。今年以來累計流入達$398億，為歷來同期次高。較高殖利率、良好信用品質，以及即將到來的夏季再投資需求，協助市場消化大量新市政債。

三井住友金融集團（SMFG）完成¥3,000億、兩個分券的AT1發行，獲約¥3,900億訂單，主要買家為壽險及信託銀行。兩個分券分別可在5.25年與10.25年後贖回，利差都比三菱日聯4月發行的可比分券低2個基點。若資本比率觸及門檻，債券可能轉換為股權，投資人的順位遠低於優先債權人。

在SMFG發行前，日本AT1發行量已較去年同期增加至逾四倍，達¥7,100億。銀行在首次贖回日前再融資，並為企業放款補充資本；預期日本央行升息，也促使發行人在基準利率及重設成本進一步增加前先行籌資。到期贖回帶來再投資需求，次順位債供給有限，同樣有利SMFG的銷售。

法國農業信貸銀行的¥1,065億、七個分券武士債，則付出較高利差。其5年期A+評等債券定價為TONA中價交換利率加58個基點，票息2.454%；三井住友銀行4月發行、評等較低的A級債券，利差僅28個基點，約為前者的一半。截至5月28日，海外借款人在武士債市場已發行¥6,627億，為七年來同期最高。日圓殖利率上升吸引收益型買家，但他們仍不願拉長天期，較偏好利差較寬的中期債券。較高評等並不保證海外發行人能取得比本國銀行便宜的資金。

週末報導顯示，美國市場接下來有更大的融資考驗。摩根大通牽頭的銀行團正以長期債務取代Warner Bros.的$150億過橋融資，並在一週內兩度擴大B類定期貸款。訂單超過$300億，受惠於借款人約BB等級的信用，以及槓桿貸款供給不足。

更大規模的Paramount Skydance融資，暫定由約$300億投資等級債、$120億高收益債及$75億貸款組成，發行時間仍未確定。Ellison家族公開承諾，必要時將注資，使槓桿符合預測，協助Paramount爭取投資等級評等。過橋融資的再融資需求強勁，卻不代表整筆收購案各部分都已獲得足夠認購。債券部分仍取決於評等認定、股東支持，以及投資人承接集中於媒體業的大額債務的意願。美國高收益債發行量已較2025年同期增加逾35%，最終成交條件將比週五基金的小幅上漲，更能看出大額信用供給的承接能力。

## 各國央行在通膨與成長之間權衡

歐洲通膨數據加強了緊縮理由。5月整體通膨年增率在法國升至2.8%、義大利3.3%、西班牙3.6%。德國放緩至2.7%，部分來自暫時性燃油稅減免及食品降價，但基本價格壓力及企業調價意願仍較強。市場繼續預期歐洲央行升息0.25個百分點，並在年內再調高一次。

義大利央行總裁Fabio Panetta表示，衝突持續、燃油庫存下降及通膨預期上升，支持重新調整政策；但他也指出，尚未出現薪資螺旋上升，中期通膨預期仍穩定。保加利亞央行總裁Dimitar Radev則警告，若預期失控才行動，代價可能更高。法國需求轉弱、義大利經濟可能停滯，使決策更難；義大利公共債務超過GDP的130%，也承受不起忽視融資成本的緊縮。首次升息的理由，比連續多次升息更明確。

日本2年期公債標售需求降溫，投資人仍在評估央行政策正常化。投標倍數由前次5.24倍降至3.7倍，接近過去12個月平均的3.74倍，標售尾差為12月以來最大。發行仍順利完成，但殖利率本週已下降，買家不急於追價。即使短端殖利率處於數十年高點，再升息及央行減少購債的風險仍在。

前一期提過的東京通膨數據，與這次標售形成對照。不含生鮮食品的核心CPI年增率降至1.3%，為四年來最低；扣除生鮮食品與能源後則上升1.6%。補貼壓低通膨之際，服務價格仍漲1.1%，不含生鮮食品的食品價格上漲4.1%。日圓在每$1兌¥159附近，加上已宣布的食品調價，使成本轉嫁疑慮未退。隔夜指數交換仍反映近期升息機率約77%；本國債券收益吸引力增加，也提高日本投資人選擇外國債券的門檻。

加拿大的成長數據更直接支持殖利率下降。第一季支出面GDP大致持平，換算年化季增率為負0.1%，遠低於預期的成長1.5%；前一季修正後為萎縮1.0%。住宅投資年化下降7.9%。3月按產業計算的產出減少0.1%，其中商品生產下降0.8%，服務增加0.1%。不過，4月初估成長0.4%，意味第二季起步較好，為疲弱的季度數據提供一些緩衝。

澳洲的投資前景則指向更強的資金需求。資料中心投資規劃超過A$1,550億，相當於全年產出的5.6%，估計可支持約40萬個工作機會；另有約A$2,000億潔淨能源計畫，增加未來對勞力與融資的需求。即使生產力最終改善，建設期間的投資需求仍支持較高中性利率的論點。澳洲央行今年已升息三次，現金利率達4.35%。

週末又有官員更新看法。英國央行決策官員Catherine Mann週六警告，過去相對穩定的通膨環境，已被更容易受到衝擊的時代取代；市場預期英國年底前升息25個基點。週日，歐洲央行官員Alvaro Santos Pereira主張更快行動，Luis de Guindos則表示供給衝擊會先影響通膨、之後才傷及成長。即將卸任的克羅埃西亞央行總裁Boris Vujcic預期，服務及食品漲價放慢，將使通膨從4月歐元區最高的5.8%回落，但能源仍受地緣政治牽動。各國差異意味首次政策回應之後，是否有必要發展為連續緊縮，仍需觀察。

## 尚比亞買回案帶動債價，新興市場各有課題

尚比亞政府提出買回債務後，2053年到期債券大漲5.9美分至79.6美分，漲幅創紀錄，也是週五表現最好的新興市場主權美元債。現金買回要約涵蓋$13.6億階梯式票息債券，6月5日前應賣者，每$1,000面額可取得$780，之後降為$740。

若尚比亞連續兩個半年期達到IMF綜合指標門檻，票息可能由0.5%升至7.5%。次月另有$250萬利息到期，在票息調高前買回，可降低未來債務成本。若參與率達75%，便可啟動剩餘債券清理條款。這些具體條件使債價漲幅遠大於整體市場；EMB當日上漲0.21%，主要受惠於美元走軟與油價下跌，減輕硬通貨融資及能源進口成本。

其他地區的新融資規劃，著眼於較長期需求。南非公布綠色、社會及永續融資框架，作為未來十年ZAR3.7兆去碳化資金需求的一部分。印度海事貸款機構Sagarmala Finance正籌備該國首檔藍色債券，規模上限₹100億，納入全年₹300億的本地債券計畫。該公司約12年期的貸款，過去靠平均僅3.5年的銀行借款支應；新債除了吸引主題投資，也可改善資產負債期限錯配。兩項計畫均尚未完成發行。

印度財政部週六警告，油價高、盧比貶值、上游成本增加，以及季風可能偏弱，都需要持續警戒。4月批發物價年增率由3.88%加速至8.30%，高於預期的5.50%，但零售通膨仍低於印度央行4%目標。當月盧比曾在每$1兌₹97附近交易，接近紀錄低點。荷莫茲海峽的能源運輸受阻，可能從進口及生產成本傳向消費物價，壓縮政策支撐經濟成長的空間。

中國週日公布的官方製造業PMI降至50.0，生產指數仍在51.2的擴張水準，新訂單卻降至49.9；非製造業指數也僅回升至50.1。訂單動能偏弱，使商品進口國與出口國難以單純受惠於能源降價。即使美國殖利率下降、美元走軟有利債券報酬，仰賴貿易現金流的財政或準主權借款人，信用前景仍可能轉差。

聯準會理事Christopher Waller週日談到另一條較長期的影響。美元穩定幣發行人通常以美元或美國國庫券等流動資產作為準備；他認為，採用這些工具的國家可能如同採取固定匯率，將美國貨幣條件引入國內。使用範圍擴大，可能增加短期美債需求，也讓聯準會政策影響更廣，即使當地經濟需要不同政策。外匯準備、監管及幣別錯配風險則不會因此消失。

## 前瞻市場意涵

接下來的美國數據，將有助判斷本週漲勢能否從油價帶來的通膨緩解，延伸至更廣泛的實質利率下降。製造業ISM於6月1日10:00美東時間公布，之後是6月2日4月JOLTS、6月3日ADP與服務業ISM、6月4日初領失業救濟金，以及6月5日08:30的就業報告。訂單、聘僱廣度及支付價格，將比週五貿易與庫存數據更完整呈現需求。若非農就業增加低於紐約聯邦住宅貸款銀行調查的9.5萬人，或失業率高於4.3%，同時訂單轉弱、價格降溫，將有利實質殖利率續降，尤其是2至5年期。需求有韌性、價格壓力持續，則會支持Schmid保留升息選項的立場。

歐元區HICP初值將於6月2日05:00美東時間公布，在歐洲央行6月10日至11日決策之前。富國銀行預測整體與核心年增率分別為3.3%與2.5%。若服務或非能源商品普遍加速，尤其數字高於這些預測，將加強進一步緊縮的理由，對歐洲殖利率及長期美債形成壓力。若漲價集中於能源、薪資穩定、其他物價放緩，Panetta的審慎立場就更有依據。

印度央行將於6月5日00:30美東時間公布決策，日本央行則在6月15日至16日開會。匯率轉弱與價格轉嫁擴大，都會減少央行暫不回應能源衝擊的空間。日本除了是否實現市場已反映約77%機率的升息，更重要的是官員對之後政策的指引。

美國財政部6月3日流動性支持買回涵蓋20至30年期名目附息公債，上限$20億，6月4日交割；6月4日現金管理操作涵蓋一個月至兩年期附息公債，上限$125億，6月5日交割。月底資金流消退後，報價、交割及國庫券交易情況將反映中介融資是否仍然順暢。

尚未排定時間的Paramount融資，則考驗企業債承接能力。訂單來源廣、定價調整有限，且能維持擬議的投資等級與高收益債分配，將顯示投資人願意承接收購槓桿。若需要大幅讓利、縮減債券部分，或更多債務留在交易商手中，就意味企業與主權供給更激烈地競逐融資能力。尚比亞6月5日提前應賣截止日，提供另一項較明確的主權債觀察點：參與率將決定能否達到75%的剩餘債券清理門檻。

overall_summary.headline: 伊朗決策未明，美國公債回吐部分漲幅
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國公債在強勁的一週後，以天期分化作收。5年期殖利率下降2個基點至4.13%，10年期維持4.45%，30年期則上升1個基點至4.99%。市場期待伊朗局勢有進展，油價因此下跌；但總統會議結束後仍未作出決定，債券回吐部分盤中漲幅。留下的利多主要是通膨補償下降，而非長期實質殖利率降低。

月底指數調整帶來大量需求，$3,240億新附息公債納入主要指標。貿易與存貨數據卻好壞參半，聯準會官員對能源通膨應觀察多久也意見不同。交換市場仍反映年底前約15個基點的緊縮幅度。歐洲通膨及日本央行正常化前的觀望情緒，同樣增加長債的不確定性。

信用市場認購金額大，但仍挑選條件。市政債基金吸金，日本AT1銷售順利，法國農業信貸銀行的武士債利差卻高於評等較低的本國銀行。Paramount融資將考驗貸款及不同評等債券的需求。尚比亞擬議買回案帶動個別主權債大漲，遠勝新興市場整體的小幅上揚；未來票息成本與剩餘債券清理門檻，是投資人是否參與的關鍵。
overall_summary.summary: 油價下降與月底買盤有利短中期美國公債，長債卻小幅下跌。美國數據好壞參半、政策仍有不確定性，長期實質殖利率也上升，限制整體漲勢。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Lower oil helped Treasuries finish a strong week, but Friday's gains faded as hopes for a US-Iran agreement ran ahead of a decision. The 5-year yield fell 2 basis points to 4.13%, the 10-year was unchanged at 4.45%, and the 30-year edged up to 4.99%. Inflation compensation eased while longer-term real yields rose, leaving the recovery concentrated in shorter and intermediate maturities.

Month-end buying gave the market an unusually large technical lift: $324 billion of notes and bonds entered a major Treasury index. Mixed trade and inventory figures offered less encouragement for a sustained rally, and Fed officials kept open the possibility of tighter policy even as some argued for looking through a temporary energy shock. Swaps still priced roughly 15 basis points of tightening by year-end.

Capital remained available across credit markets, though on markedly different terms. Municipal funds drew strong inflows, Japanese banks attracted demand for subordinated capital, and a large media-acquisition financing began testing appetite across loans and rating categories. Zambia's buyback proposal produced a much sharper sovereign move than the quiet rise in broad EM debt. In Europe and Japan, inflation and impending policy decisions continued to complicate the outlook for bondholders.

## Oil Relief Fades at the Long End

Treasuries initially rallied toward weekly lows in yield after President Donald Trump said a meeting on Iran was under way. Expectations that Middle East supply could normalize had already pulled benchmark oil to a six-week low. Prices gave back part of the gain after reports that Trump left the meeting without a final decision. The 30-year Treasury yield touched 4.96% before closing 3 basis points above that low.

WTI fell 1.73% to $87.36 and Brent dropped 1.77% to $92.05. Cheaper crude reduced the near-term inflation impulse, but its dependence on an unresolved geopolitical outcome left investors reluctant to extend the bond rally. At the close, the 2-year yield was down 1 basis point at 3.98%, the 5-year down 2 at 4.13%, the 10-year flat at 4.45%, and the 30-year up 1 at 4.99%. The 2s10s curve steepened 1 basis point to 47 and 2s30s widened 2 to 101. The 5-year sector's outperformance pushed the 2s5s10s butterfly down 3 basis points to -17; 2s10s30s was unchanged at -7.

The 10-year breakeven declined 1 basis point to 2.38%, offset by a 1-basis-point increase in the real yield to 2.07%. Real yields on 5- and 7-year TIPS held at 1.61% and 1.83%, while 20- and 30-year yields each rose 1 basis point to 2.49% and 2.71%. That was a change from Thursday's real-yield-led gains. Over the full week, however, the 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year nominal yields still fell 15, 14, 11 and 8 basis points, respectively, recovering part of the war-driven selloff.

April's trade figures showed stronger flows in both directions. The advance goods deficit narrowed to $82.4 billion from a revised $85.3 billion, compared with an $86.5 billion consensus. Exports rose $8.5 billion to $219.7 billion and imports increased $5.6 billion to $302.1 billion. The smaller deficit improved the net-export arithmetic for GDP without indicating a collapse in domestic demand.

Inventories gave a less consistent account of spending. Wholesale stocks rose 0.5%, below the 0.8% forecast and March's revised 1.5% increase. Retail inventories grew 0.7%, above the 0.4% consensus, with a 0.6% rise outside motor vehicles and 0.9% at vehicle dealers. The accumulation could support near-term GDP, but did not settle whether final demand was keeping pace.

Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said inflation remained too hot after April PCE prices rose 3.8% from a year earlier. Officials should retain flexibility to move rates in either direction, he said. He described the labor market as balanced: slower labor-force growth could accommodate weaker hiring without a rise in unemployment. His assessment left room for an inflation-driven increase even without an overheated jobs market.

Michelle Bowman favored looking through temporary energy inflation, warning that additional restraint could unnecessarily weaken activity and employment. A longer conflict, sustained oil prices or broader PCE pass-through would change that calculation. Mary Daly saw no urgency to adjust rates, while Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson described a series of price shocks without evidence of a structural inflation shift. Together, the comments left investors weighing the persistence of the shock rather than a clear policy commitment.

Passive demand was more immediate. About $324 billion of newly sold notes and bonds joined a major Treasury index at 4 p.m. New York time, compared with roughly $240 billion at each of the March and April month-ends. Futures volume surged as funds rebalanced. Prices rose around the index change, helping intermediate maturities, but did not regain their intraday highs.

In a strategy update released shortly after 5 p.m., Deutsche Bank projected a December peak of 4.70% for the 10-year yield, raising its previous year-end forecast from near the prevailing 4.45%. The bank expected the Fed to have finished cutting and to hold at a long-run neutral setting. That differed from market pricing of roughly a 55% chance of a hike by year-end, although both outlooks left less scope for a sustained decline in yields.

Equities finished higher, with the S&P 500 up 0.22% and the Nasdaq 100 up 0.36%. Semiconductors were essentially unchanged after a strong week, and the VIX fell 2.67% to 15.32. The dollar index slipped 0.11% to 98.91, easing some pressure on dollar borrowers. Gold rose 1.36% to $4,560.50 despite the gains in stocks and lower volatility, as demand for protection against geopolitical and inflation uncertainty persisted.

## Strong Demand, Different Credit Terms

Credit funds posted modest gains: LQD rose 0.09%, HYG 0.10% and JNK 0.16%. Short-term funding remained steady, with coupon-equivalent bill yields between 3.68% and 3.79% and no maturity from 4 to 52 weeks moving more than 1 basis point. In primary markets, investors were committing substantial sums, but the attraction varied with yield, capital structure and scarcity.

US tax-exempt funds received about $2.3 billion in the week ended May 27, almost twice the previous week's inflow and the second-largest weekly total since 1992. Municipal ETFs accounted for roughly $1.7 billion. Year-to-date inflows reached $39.8 billion, the second-highest comparable total on record. Higher yields, strong credit quality and the approaching summer reinvestment season helped buyers absorb a heavy municipal issuance calendar.

Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group priced a ¥300 billion, two-tranche Additional Tier 1 deal against approximately ¥390 billion of orders, led by life insurers and trust banks. The tranches, callable after 5.25 and 10.25 years, each priced 2 basis points tighter than comparable Mitsubishi UFJ AT1 securities sold in April. The instruments can convert to equity if capital ratios breach their trigger, placing investors well below senior creditors.

Before the SMFG sale, Japanese AT1 issuance had more than quadrupled from a year earlier to ¥710 billion. Banks were refinancing ahead of first-call dates and building capital for corporate lending, with expectations of higher BOJ rates encouraging them to issue before benchmark and reset costs climbed further. Redemptions created replacement demand, and limited subordinated supply helped SMFG's placement.

Credit Agricole paid a wider spread in its ¥106.5 billion, seven-tranche Samurai offering. The 5-year A+ notes priced at 58 basis points over TONA mid-swaps with a 2.454% coupon—about twice the 28-basis-point spread on lower-rated A notes issued by Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. in April. Overseas borrowers had sold ¥662.7 billion of Samurai bonds through May 28, the busiest comparable period in seven years. Higher yen yields drew income buyers, but their reluctance to extend maturity favored wider-spread intermediate bonds. A stronger rating alone did not secure cheaper funding than a domestic issuer's.

Weekend reporting pointed to a much larger test in the US. A JPMorgan-led bank group was replacing a $15 billion Warner Bros. bridge facility with longer-term debt. It increased the term loan B twice during the week after receiving more than $30 billion of orders, helped by the borrower's BB-area credit profile and a shortage of leveraged-loan supply.

The broader Paramount Skydance financing was tentatively divided into about $30 billion of investment-grade bonds, $12 billion of high-yield notes and $7.5 billion of loans; sale timing remained unsettled. The Ellison family publicly pledged to inject capital if needed to keep leverage aligned with forecasts, supporting Paramount's effort to secure investment-grade ratings. Strong demand for the bridge refinancing did not establish demand for every part of the acquisition package. The bond portions still depended on rating treatment, sponsor support and investors' willingness to take a large concentration of media debt. With US junk issuance already more than 35% above the comparable 2025 period, the eventual terms would provide a larger measure of credit appetite than Friday's small fund gains.

## Central Banks Face Inflation and Growth Crosscurrents

European inflation strengthened the case for tighter policy. May headline readings accelerated to 2.8% in France, 3.3% in Italy and 3.6% in Spain. Germany slowed to 2.7%, helped partly by temporary fuel-tax relief and cheaper food, while underlying pressure and companies' pricing intentions remained firmer. Markets continued to expect a quarter-point ECB increase and another move later in the year.

Bank of Italy Governor Fabio Panetta said persistent conflict, declining fuel stocks and rising expectations warranted a policy recalibration. He also noted the absence of a wage spiral and still-anchored medium-term expectations. Bulgarian central-bank chief Dimitar Radev warned that acting late could prove more costly if expectations loosened. Weaker French demand and the possibility of Italian stagnation complicated the choice; Italy's debt above 130% of GDP also made higher funding costs consequential. The case for an initial increase was firmer than the case for an extended sequence.

Japan's 2-year auction drew less enthusiastic demand as investors weighed BOJ normalization. The bid-to-cover ratio fell to 3.7 from 5.24 at the previous sale, near its 12-month average of 3.74, and the tail was the widest since December. The auction cleared smoothly, but yields' decline over the week had reduced the urgency to buy. Another policy increase and smaller BOJ purchases remained risks even with short yields at multi-decade highs.

The Tokyo inflation figures described in the previous edition supplied an important contrast to that auction. Core CPI excluding fresh food had slowed to 1.3%, its weakest pace in four years, and the measure excluding fresh food and energy rose 1.6%. Beneath the subsidy effects, services rose 1.1% and food excluding fresh items increased 4.1%. The yen near 159 per dollar and announced food-price increases sustained pass-through concerns. OIS still assigned roughly a 77% chance to a near-term BOJ increase, while more attractive domestic yields raised the hurdle for Japanese investment in foreign bonds.

Canada offered a clearer growth argument for lower yields. Q1 expenditure-based GDP was essentially flat, or a 0.1% annualized contraction, far below the 1.5% consensus after a revised 1.0% contraction in Q4. Residential investment fell at a 7.9% annualized pace. March industry output declined 0.1%, as goods production fell 0.8% and services rose 0.1%. An advance estimate of 0.4% growth in April provided a better start to Q2, tempering the weak quarterly picture.

Australia's investment outlook pointed toward stronger demand for capital. A projected data-center pipeline exceeding A$155 billion, or 5.6% of annual output, was estimated to support about 400,000 jobs. Roughly A$200 billion of clean-energy projects added to the prospective call on labor and financing. Even if productivity eventually improved, that investment demand supported the argument for a higher neutral rate. The RBA cash rate was already 4.35% after three increases during the year.

Further policy comments arrived over the weekend. BOE policymaker Catherine Mann warned on Saturday that a more shock-prone inflation era had replaced the previous period of stability; markets expected a 25-basis-point UK increase by year-end. On Sunday, ECB member Alvaro Santos Pereira favored faster action, while Luis de Guindos said the supply shock would affect inflation before growth. Outgoing Croatian central-bank Governor Boris Vujcic expected inflation to ease from April's euro-area-high 5.8% as services and food pressure slowed, although energy remained exposed to geopolitics. The differences across countries mattered for how far an initial ECB response might develop into a tightening cycle.

## Zambia's Tender Leads a Mixed Emerging-Market Picture

Zambia's 2053 bond jumped a record 5.9 cents to 79.6, Friday's best performance among emerging-market sovereign dollar bonds, after the government offered to buy back the debt. The cash tender covered a $1.36 billion step-up issue and offered $780 per $1,000 to holders tendering by June 5, falling to $740 afterward.

The coupon could rise to 7.5% from 0.5% if Zambia met the IMF composite-indicator threshold for two consecutive semiannual periods. With a $2.5 million interest payment due the following month, a repurchase before the step-up would reduce future servicing costs. Participation of 75% would activate the cleanup provision. Those bond-specific terms drove a much larger move than the broad EM market: EMB rose 0.21%, supported by a softer dollar and lower oil, which eased hard-currency funding and energy import costs.

New financing plans elsewhere addressed longer-term needs. South Africa published a green, social and sustainability framework as part of a 3.7 trillion rand decarbonization funding requirement over the coming decade. India's maritime lender Sagarmala Finance was preparing the country's first blue bond, seeking up to 10 billion rupees within a 30 billion-rupee annual local-bond plan. Its roughly 12-year loans had been funded by bank borrowing averaging only 3.5 years, giving the proposed issue a practical role in reducing the maturity mismatch. Neither plan yet represented completed issuance.

India's finance ministry warned on Saturday that high crude prices, rupee depreciation, rising upstream costs and the risk of a weak monsoon required continued vigilance. Wholesale inflation accelerated to 8.30% in April from 3.88%, exceeding a 5.50% consensus, even though retail inflation remained below the RBI's 4% target. The rupee had traded near a record low of about 97 per dollar during the month. Energy disruption around the Strait of Hormuz could pass from import and producer costs into consumer inflation, leaving less room for policy to support growth.

China's official manufacturing PMI, released Sunday, fell to 50.0. Production remained in expansion at 51.2, but new orders slipped to 49.9; the non-manufacturing index rose to only 50.1. Weaker order momentum complicated the benefit of cheaper energy for commodity importers and exporters alike. Fiscal and quasi-sovereign borrowers relying on trade cash flow could face a less favorable credit outlook even if lower US yields and a softer dollar supported bond returns.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller discussed a separate, longer-run channel on Sunday. Dollar stablecoin issuers generally back their liabilities with liquid assets such as dollars and Treasury bills. Countries adopting those instruments could import US monetary conditions much as they would under a fixed exchange rate, he argued. Wider use could increase demand for short Treasuries and extend the reach of Fed policy, including where domestic economic conditions called for a different stance. Reserve, regulatory and currency-mismatch risks would remain.

## Forward Market Significance

The coming US data will help determine whether the week's recovery can extend beyond oil-related inflation relief. Manufacturing ISM is due June 1 at 10:00 ET, followed by April JOLTS on June 2, ADP and services ISM on June 3, claims on June 4, and the employment report on June 5 at 08:30 ET. Orders, hiring breadth and prices paid will give a fuller account of demand than Friday's trade and inventory figures. Payroll growth below the FHLB New York survey's 95,000 estimate or unemployment above 4.3%, alongside weaker orders and cooler prices, would favor further real-yield declines, particularly in the 2- to 5-year sector. Resilient activity and persistent price pressure would preserve Schmid's case for keeping an increase available.

Euro-area flash HICP is due June 2 at 05:00 ET, ahead of the ECB's June 10-11 decision. Wells Fargo forecasts headline and core rates of 3.3% and 2.5%. A broader acceleration in services or non-energy goods, especially with readings above those estimates, would strengthen the argument for further tightening and put pressure on European yields and long Treasuries. An energy-concentrated rise with stable wages and softer underlying prices would give more weight to Panetta's caution.

The RBI decision follows on June 5 at 00:30 ET, with the BOJ meeting June 15-16. Currency weakness and broader price pass-through would reduce room to look through the energy shock. For Japan, the question is whether the BOJ follows through on the increase already assigned about a 77% probability, and what it signals beyond that meeting.

Treasury's June 3 liquidity-support buyback covers 20- to 30-year nominal coupons, capped at $2 billion and settling June 4. Its June 4 cash-management operation covers one-month to two-year coupons, capped at $12.5 billion with June 5 settlement. Offers, settlement and bill trading will show whether intermediation remains comfortable as the month-end flows subside.

The still-unscheduled Paramount financing brings a parallel test for corporate balance sheets. Broad books, limited pricing revisions and preservation of the proposed investment-grade/high-yield split would support the view that investors can absorb the acquisition leverage. Large concessions, a smaller bond component or more debt left with dealers would indicate greater competition between corporate and sovereign supply for financing capacity. Zambia's June 5 early-tender deadline provides a more specific sovereign milestone, with participation determining whether the 75% cleanup threshold can be reached.

section_summaries.summary: Oil fell and month-end buying supported Treasuries, but an unresolved Iran decision and firmer real yields left the long end behind. Credit markets remained open, with demand depending on the issuer and financing terms.

section_summaries.section_title: Oil Relief Fades at the Long End
section_summaries.summary: The Treasury rally faded after the Iran meeting ended without a decision. Inflation compensation eased, long-term real yields rose, and unusually large index buying helped intermediate maturities despite mixed data and two-way Fed policy risks.

Municipal inflows and Japanese bank-capital orders showed substantial demand. Credit Agricole's wider Samurai pricing and the still-pending Paramount package highlighted the importance of issuer familiarity, ratings, maturity and sponsor support.

section_summaries.section_title: Central Banks Face Inflation and Growth Crosscurrents
section_summaries.summary: Higher European inflation favored an ECB increase, while Japan's auction reflected caution ahead of normalization. Weak Canadian growth and Australia's investment pipeline pointed in opposite directions for bond yields.

section_summaries.section_title: Zambia's Tender Leads a Mixed Emerging-Market Picture
section_summaries.summary: Zambia's tender sent its long bond sharply higher. Elsewhere, labeled-finance plans addressed funding needs, while India's inflation risks and China's weaker orders complicated the benefit of lower oil and a softer dollar.

US ISM and labor reports, euro-area inflation and Asian policy decisions will test the rally. Treasury buybacks, Paramount's financing and Zambia's tender offer more specific evidence on funding and creditor demand.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries ended a strong week with a split close. The 5-year yield fell 2 basis points to 4.13%, but the 10-year held at 4.45% and the 30-year rose 1 basis point to 4.99%. Oil dropped as investors anticipated progress on Iran, then bonds pared their intraday gains when a presidential meeting ended without a decision. Falling inflation compensation, rather than lower long-term real yields, accounted for the remaining relief.

Month-end index demand supplied a large buyer, with $324 billion of new notes and bonds entering a major benchmark. Trade and inventory data were mixed, and Fed officials differed over how long to look through energy inflation. Swaps still priced about 15 basis points of tightening by year-end. European inflation and caution ahead of BOJ normalization added to the uncertainty for longer-dated bonds.

Credit demand remained substantial but selective. Municipal funds attracted large inflows, Japanese AT1 sold well, and Credit Agricole paid a wider Samurai spread than a lower-rated domestic bank. The Paramount financing will test demand across loans and rating categories. Zambia's proposed tender drove a much larger sovereign gain than the modest rise in broad EM debt, with future coupon costs and the cleanup threshold central to participation.
overall_summary.summary: Lower oil and month-end buying helped shorter and intermediate Treasuries, while the long bond slipped. Mixed US data, persistent policy uncertainty and firmer long-term real yields prevented a broader advance.
